Earlier this month, OpenAI released the first GPT-6 model paired with Astra. Now GPT-6 is expanding with two new variants: GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna.

GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna are now available

According to a release note from the ChatGPT desktop app, GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna use fewer tokens at inference than the comparable GPT-5.6 models.

GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna are rolling out across Codex and ChatGPT Work, with lower token pricing than the previous-generation GPT-5.6. Sol is suited to complex coding and agentic workflows, while Luna is built for focused, high-volume work. Both models will become available to Plus, Pro, Business, Enterprise and Edu users over time. Free and Go users can access Luna in the desktop app. Actual availability depends on the rollout and workspace settings; Enterprise admins must enable the new models. Within ChatGPT, the two models are available in Work and Codex, but not in Chat.

Note that there is no GPT-6 Terra model this time. As expected, OpenAI is dropping the medium-sized variant and keeping only three: Terra (small), Sol (large) and Astra (extra-large).

Below is OpenAI's official announcement:

Although the most demanding and important projects still need the full depth of Astra, work comes in different sizes, tempos and budgets. So we're extending the GPT-6 family with GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna. GPT-6 Astra opened up a new generation of intelligence—and these two new models spread the benefits of that intelligence further by delivering even better cost efficiency. We trained GPT-6 Sol and Luna using a similar approach to GPT-6 Astra, bringing Astra's state-of-the-art performance in professional work, factual accuracy, coding, computer use and alignment to faster, more affordable models.

The company describes its two newest models as more capable than the GPT-5.6 versions, while also more affordable than Astra (and the GPT-5.6 models they replace). For example, the GPT-6 versions of Sol and Luna are 50% cheaper than the GPT-5.6 versions.
